0: TOWN OF VERNONBURG ORDINANCE O2026-01.B Establishment of a Records Retention and Management Program STATE OF GEORGIA } TOWN OF VERNONBURG } AN ORDINANCE BY THE INTENDANT AND COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF VERNONBURG, GEORGIA, AMENDING THE CODE OF ORDINANCES OF THE TOWN OF VERNONBURG, GEORGIA, TO ESTABLISH A RECORDS RETENTION AND MANAGEMENT PROGRAM AND TO ADOPT THE GEORGIA ARCHIVES LOCAL GOVERNMENT RECORDS RETENTION SCHEDULE THROUGH THE ADDITION OF CHAPTER 6 - RECORDS MANAGEMENT. WHEREAS, the duly elected governing authority of the Town of Vernonburg, Georgia, is authorized by O.C.G.A. § 36-35-3 to adopt ordinances relating to its property, affairs, and local government; and WHEREAS, the Intendant and Council have the authority to amend the Town's ordinances from time to time and where necessary to maintain adequate regulations; WHEREAS, the Georgia Records Act (O.C.G.A. § 50‑18‑90 et seq.) requires local governments to adopt and maintain a records management program, including a records retention schedule and provisions for records maintenance and security; and WHEREAS, all records created or received in the performance of public duty and paid for by public funds are public property and may only be destroyed pursuant to an approved retention schedule; and WHEREAS, the Georgia Archives publishes Retention Schedules for Local Government Records that have been approved by the State Records Committee and updated periodically; NOW THEREFORE, THE INTENDANT AND COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF VERNONBURG, GEORGIA, HEREBY ORDAIN, that the Code of Ordinances of the Town of Vernonburg, Georgia, is hereby amended by adding Chapter 5. ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS, Article II. Records Management, which reads as follows: I.
1: The purpose of this ordinance is to provide for the systematic retention, maintenance, preservation, and disposal of all records of the Town of Vernonburg consistent with Georgia law and best records management practices.

2 For the purposes of this chapter: Record or Public Record means any document, paper, letter, map, book, photograph, or other materials regardless of physical form created, received, or maintained by the Town of Vernonburg in pursuance of public business. Retention Schedule means the Local Government Records Retention Schedule approved by the Georgia Archives and the State Records Committee, as amended from time to time. Records Officer means the official designated by the Town to administer the records management program.
3: The Town Clerk shall be designated as the Records Officer for the Town, responsible for overseeing the records management program, including: 1. Maintaining the inventory of records series; 2. Coordinating retention and destruction actions; 3. Ensuring compliance with this Ordinance and state law; 4. Serving as liaison with Georgia Archives. In the absence of a Town Clerk, the Intendant may designate a designee or deputy, or serve as Records Officer themselves.
4:
- (a) The Town of Vernonburg hereby adopts the Georgia Archives Local Government Records Retention Schedule, including all categories and minimum retention periods established therein, as the official retention schedule for all municipal records of the Town. Retention periods established in the Georgia Archives schedule shall serve as the minimum requirements for retention; the Town may retain records longer when required or desirable for legal, fiscal, historical, or administrative purposes. (b) Copies of the current Georgia Archives Local Government Records Retention Schedule shall be maintained in the office of the Town Clerk and/or City Attorney and made available for public inspection. (c) A record may not be destroyed, altered, transferred, or otherwise disposed of unless authorized by the applicable retention period in the adopted schedule or as otherwise permitted by law. 5: The Town may maintain a records management plan to support the implementation of this ordinance and to ensure proper maintenance, retention, and security of town records. Such a plan may include, but is not limited to: 1. An inventory of record series; 2. Procedures for storage, access, and protection of records; 3. Guidelines for the disposal of records in accordance with the adopted retention schedule; 4. Measures to safeguard vital records and support disaster recovery. The Records Officer shall oversee any such plan, if adopted, and may update it as necessary to facilitate compliance with this ordinance and applicable state law.
6: - (a) No record may be destroyed except in accordance with the retention periods set forth in the Georgia Archives schedule and with proper documentation authorizing the destruction. (b) The Records Officer shall prepare and maintain records destruction logs, including record series name, retention period, date of destruction, and method of destruction.
7: Records maintained in electronic, magnetic, or other digital formats shall be retained for the same periods as required for paper records. Electronic records are considered official records of the Town and are subject to all requirements of this ordinance and the Georgia Records Act (O.C.G.A. § 50-18-90 et seq.), including retention, maintenance, and authorized destruction.
8: Nothing in this ordinance shall authorize the destruction of records that are: 1. Subject to pending litigation or legal hold; 2. Necessary to protect the legal rights of the Town or any officer; 3. Required to be retained longer by other governmental requirement.
